resp.how.title: How to get it
resp.how.1: Get a Social Insurance Number for your child
resp.how.1d: You need one too, if you don’t have one yet.
resp.how.2d: Most banks, credit unions and investment firms offer RESPs. Compare providers before you choose.
resp.how.3: Open the RESP and apply for the grant and bond
resp.how.3d: Name your child as the beneficiary. The provider applies for the benefits for you.
resp.how.4: Put money in, then check the deposits
resp.how.4d: The grant needs contributions; the bond doesn’t. The grant is usually deposited within 6 to 8 weeks of a contribution, once your application is processed.
resp.tip.old.title: At 16 or 17, the grant has a catch.
resp.tip.old.body: It’s only paid if, by the end of the year your child turned 15, at least {total} was put in, or at least {yearly} a year in any {years} years. This plan assumes a new RESP.
resp.tip.more.title: Put in {more} more a year to get the full grant.
resp.tip.more.body: The grant matches {rate} of the first {max} you put in each year: {grant}.
resp.tip.catch.title: You may be able to catch up {room} of missed grant.
resp.tip.catch.body: This assumes your child hasn’t received any grant yet. Unused grant carries forward: put in {amount} in a year to get up to {grant} of grant that year.
resp.tip.clb.title: Your child may get the Canada Learning Bond: up to {max}.
resp.tip.clb.body: You don’t have to put in any money. Ask your RESP provider to apply; past years count too. You can request it until your child turns {parentAge}; after that, they can request it themselves until {age}.
resp.tip.cap.title: You’ve reached the {max} lifetime limit on contributions.
resp.tip.full.title: You’re collecting the full grant each year.
resp.tip.full.body: More than this still grows tax-sheltered, but doesn’t earn more grant.
resp.clbHint: Lower-income families can also get the Canada Learning Bond (up to {max}, no contribution needed).
resp.clbLimits: The family income limit is {few} for 1 to 3 children. With 4 children, income must be under {four}; with 5, under {five}.

cmp.hero.best.tfsa: Here, the *TFSA* leaves you the most.
cmp.hero.best.rrsp: Here, the *RRSP* leaves you the most.
cmp.hero.best.fhsa: For a first home, the *FHSA* leaves you the most.
cmp.hero.best.hbp: For a first home, the RRSP’s *Home Buyers’ Plan* gives you the most, but you pay it back.
cmp.why.fhsa: A deduction going in, no tax coming out, and nothing to pay back. The RRSP’s Home Buyers’ Plan matches it only if you repay it over {years} years.
cmp.why.higher: At {now} now and {later} later, the RRSP’s deduction saves more than you’d pay on the way out.
cmp.why.lower: At {now} now and {later} later, you’d pay more tax taking RRSP money out than the deduction saves, so the TFSA comes out ahead.
cmp.why.same: With the same tax rate now and later, the TFSA and RRSP end up equal. The TFSA stays more flexible.
